translationRepairs: The talented lady Shimozhi bore Yun Sheng, Prince of Kui.
Lady Shimo, a cairen, bore Yun Sheng, Prince of Kui.

才人石抹氏 is a consort rank plus the Shimo clan-name, not a personal name Shimozhi. The proposed cairen gloss is right, but the wording should follow the neighboring zhaoyi pattern rather than 'the cairen of the Shimo clan.'
Talented Lady Shimozhi bore Prince of Kui Yun Sheng.
Cairen Shimo bore Prince of Kui Yun Sheng.
The original treats 石抹氏 as the personal name Shimozhi. 'Lady of Talents' is not a natural literal for 才人; the neighboring literals use rank plus clan (Zhaoyi Liang, Primary consort Li).

Prince Wu Yongcheng, who was administering Zhending, and Prince Sui Yongsheng, commissioner of the Dingwu army, came late to the mourning. Each was docked a month's pay, and their chief administrators were flogged fifty times.

Yong Cheng, Prince of Wu, who was administering Zhending, and Yong Sheng, Prince of Sui, commissioner of the Dingwu army, came late to the mourning. Each was docked a month's pay, and their chief administrators were flogged fifty times.
吳王永成 and 隋王永升 are fief titles plus the given names Yong Cheng and Yong Sheng, not fused names Prince Wu Yongcheng and Prince Sui Yongsheng.

In the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year, while Shizong was summering at Haoshuichuan on Tianping Mountain, Xianzong died in the Central Capital. An edict ordered Prince Cao Yong Gong to look after Zhangzong and summoned Yong Zhong to the imperial camp.

In the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year, while Shizong was summering at Haoshuichuan on Tianping Mountain, Xianzong died in the Central Capital. An edict ordered Yong Gong, Prince of Cao, to look after Zhangzong and summoned Yong Zhong to the imperial camp.
曹王永功 is Yong Gong, Prince of Cao; the original 'Prince Cao Yong Gong' presents Cao as if it were part of the personal name.
In the fifth year of Mingchang Gaotuowo was executed for curse-magic and imprecation.
In the fifth year of Mingchang, Gaotuowo was executed for curse-magic and imprecation.
Without a comma, 'Mingchang Gaotuowo' reads as one name. The Chinese is the era 明昌五年 followed by the person 高陀斡.
In the twenty-fifth year he was given the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
In the twenty-fifth year he was given the rank of kaifu yitong sansi, with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
開府儀同三司 is not 太師 (Grand Preceptor). 'Commander Unequaled in Honor' imports a commander sense the Chinese does not state; keep the existing honors gloss and name the rank kaifu yitong sansi.
In the twenty-fifth year he was granted the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
In the twenty-fifth year he was granted the rank of kaifu yitong sansi (honors equal to those of the Three Excellencies).
The literal likewise invents Grand Preceptor for 開府儀同三司; the replacement names the rank and keeps the 儀同三司 honors gloss.
On Shizong's last visit to Jingdian, Yong Gong reported: "The imperial guard had only one attendant and two centurions standing watch — they had been at it a long time.
When the emperor halted at Wangjingdian, Yong Gong reported: "The imperial guard had only one attendant and two centurions standing watch — they had been at it a long time.
望京澱 is Wangjingdian, not Jingdian. 上次 is the emperor's halt (上 + 次), not 'last visit'; the proposed line still mistranslates 上次.
When Shizong last visited Jingdian, Yong Gong memorialized: "The imperial guard had only one attendant and two centurions on duty — they had served long.
When Shizong halted at Wangjingdian, Yong Gong memorialized: "The imperial guard had only one attendant and two centurions on duty — they had served long.
望京澱 is Wangjingdian. 上次 records the emperor's halt there after leaving the Central Capital, not a 'last visit.'
Zhangzong was made Prince of Yuan and given the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
Zhangzong was made Prince of Yuan and given the rank of kaifu yitong sansi, with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
加開府儀同三司 is not Grand Preceptor. Replacing Three Excellencies with Three Dukes is an unnecessary wording change; the original honors gloss already renders 儀同三司.
Zhangzong was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuan and granted the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
Zhangzong was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuan and granted the rank of kaifu yitong sansi (honors equal to the Three Excellencies).
The Grand Preceptor error is real, but 儀同三司 should keep the original 'Three Excellencies' gloss rather than switch to 'Three Dukes.'
Under Prince Wei-Shao he was given the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
Under Prince Wei-Shao he was given the rank of kaifu yitong sansi, with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
開府儀同三司 is not Grand Preceptor, but 'Opening an Office' is an awkward calque of 開府, not a usable English rank name.
During the reign of Prince of Wei-Shao he was granted Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
During the reign of Prince of Wei-Shao he was granted the rank of kaifu yitong sansi, with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
The Grand Preceptor error is real; 'Opening an Office' is not an adequate literal for the full title 開府儀同三司.
At the opening of Tianxing Shu was already bedridden. Discussing current affairs, he sighed and said: "With the military situation like this, we cannot hold out; we can only surrender.
At the opening of Tianxing, Shu was already bedridden. Discussing current affairs, he sighed and said: "With the military situation like this, we cannot hold out; we can only surrender.
天興初，璹 already separates the era from the person Shu; the missing comma makes 'Tianxing Shu' look like one name.
In the twenty-fifth year of Dading he, Zhangzong, and all the elder princes were given the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
In the twenty-fifth year of Dading he, Zhangzong, and all the elder princes were given the rank of kaifu yitong sansi, with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
大定二十五年…俱加開府儀同三司 is not a grant of Grand Preceptor. 'Opening an Office' is an awkward stand-in for the rank name.
In the twenty-fifth year of Dading he, Zhangzong, and all the elder princes were granted the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
In the twenty-fifth year of Dading he, Zhangzong, and all the elder princes were granted the rank of kaifu yitong sansi, with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
The literal repeats the Grand Preceptor error; the replacement's 'Opening an Office' calque is still not a correct title rendering.

In the twenty-fifth year, when Shizong went to the Upper Capital, Yong Cheng was left to guard the Central Capital, given charge of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and made Censor-in-Chief.

In the twenty-fifth year, when Shizong went to the Upper Capital, Yong Cheng was left to guard the Central Capital, given charge of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to the rank of kaifu yitong sansi, with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and made Censor-in-Chief.
進開府儀同三司 is not promotion to Grand Preceptor; 判吏部尚書 is already well rendered. 'Opening an Office' is not natural English for the rank.

In the twenty-fifth year, when Shizong visited the Upper Capital, Yong Cheng was ordered to remain and guard the Central Capital, to serve as Minister of Personnel, was advanced to Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and made Censor-in-Chief.

In the twenty-fifth year, when Shizong visited the Upper Capital, Yong Cheng was ordered to remain and guard the Central Capital, to administer the Ministry of Personnel, was advanced to the rank of kaifu yitong sansi, with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and made Censor-in-Chief.
判吏部尚書 is concurrent charge of the ministry, not appointment as Minister, and 開府儀同三司 is not Grand Preceptor. 'Opening an Office' remains an awkward calque.
In the twenty-sixth year he was given the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
In the twenty-sixth year he was given the rank of kaifu yitong sansi, with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
二十六年，加開府儀同三司 names the prestige rank, not 太師. The replacement is accurate and keeps the ceremonial-honors gloss.
In the twenty-sixth year he was granted the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
In the twenty-sixth year he was granted the rank of kaifu yitong sansi, with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
The literal field has the same Grand Preceptor error for 開府儀同三司; the proposed wording names the rank and preserves the honors sense.
